definitions.explanation: A supernatural being that has transformed or shapeshifted — ghosts, spirits, and creatures from Japanese folklore that take on different forms. Derived from {化|ば}ける (to transform).
Used figuratively for a person with extraordinary, almost inhuman abilities or characteristics — often in admiration of exceptional talent or physical capability.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{屋敷|やしき}→屋敷：12395_yashiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: Monsters appear in the old mansion.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、{化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{怖|こわ}かった→怖い：00864_kowai⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, I was scared of monster stories.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{様々|さまざま}→様々：01559_samazama⟧な{化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{登場|とうじょう}→登場：13625_toujou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Various monsters appear in Japanese folktales.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{化|ば}け{物|もの}だ。
{化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦みたい→みたい：10755_mitai⟧な⟦{体力|たいりょく}→体力：05318_tairyoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}→持ち主：10439_mochinushi⟧だ。
⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{記憶力|きおくりょく}→記憶力：17616_kiokuryoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{化|ば}け{物|もの}じみて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。

notes:
From ⟦{化|ば}ける→化ける：11849_bakeru⟧ (to transform) + ⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧ (thing). In Japanese folklore, {化|ば}け{物|もの} specifically refers to creatures that shapeshift or transform, such as fox and tanuki spirits. Broader than ⟦{幽霊|ゆうれい}→幽霊：10648_yuurei⟧ (ghost of a dead person).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ (a monster appears)
- {化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦みたい→みたい：10755_mitai⟧な (monster-like, freakish)
- {化|ば}け{物|もの}じみて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ (freakish, monstrous)
- {化|ば}け{物|もの}⟦{屋敷|やしき}→屋敷：12395_yashiki⟧ (haunted house)
